target_customer: Food and beverage manufacturers seeking lower calorie sugar ingredients
problem: Sugar drives obesity and diabetes risk, but reformulating foods without sugar costs texture and taste.
business_model: B2B ingredient sales plus a licensed consumer launch
product_category: Food tech, fiber derived sugar ingredient

founders.name: Tom Simmons
education: University of Cambridge, doctorate and postdoctoral research
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch 2021-02-26 says the company grew out of his Cambridge research.

founders.name: Ruben Tadmor
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; background not found.

exit.reason: City AM of 2025-08-05 reports the company entered administration and was offered for sale above 2.5 million pounds; it states no cause.

technical_complexity.rationale: Requires an enzymatic process to convert agricultural fiber into a new sugar blend and EU novel food approval, which is research grade work.

defensibility.rationale: Patented process, preliminary EU regulatory approval and unique feedstock upcycling were hard to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought it. The company reached a 2021 US launch and later administration in 2025.

market_need_then: Sugar reduction was a major food industry driver, and the founders said in 2021 that the product had preliminary EU approval.

branding.domain_note: Used supplant.com; a fetch in this session did not resolve, so current status is unknown.

identity.voice_and_tone: Positions the ingredient as a new category called sugars from fiber, with a trademark symbol on the term.

branding.brand_signature: Sugars from fiber, launched with desserts by Thomas Keller at The French Laundry in June 2021

rebrands.why: Not stated; TechCrunch 2021 describes Supplant as formerly Cambridge Glycoscience.

branding.community_and_virality: Celebrity investors Ayesha Curry and Chris Paul joined in October 2021, which drew press.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong press at the 2021 launch with a chef partner and celebrity backers, but the brand never became a consumer staple.

outcome_analysis: Supplant grew out of Cambridge research, joined YC in summer 2018, raised about $24M in 2021 and an $18M Series A tranche later that year, and launched in the US with a chef partnership. It took on a $3.6M loan and owed trade creditors $2M when it entered administration in August 2025 with about $1M of revenue at peak. City AM gives no cause, so the failure factors are inferences from the debt and thin revenue.
notes: Funding sources conflict. TechCrunch gives $24M venture financing in February 2021; another outlet reported a $15M Series A in February 2021 and an $18M Series A in October 2021, with totals from $27M to $42M in different databases, and a trade outlet first reported $25M then corrected to $18M. The February 2021 round is labeled other because TechCrunch gives no stage. The $5M seed via YC rests on City AM only and is undated. The $3.6M loan is undated. The company website could not be fetched because the host did not resolve in this session, so supplant.com has to be allowed in network settings to check it. The competitor list is empty because no source dated near summer 2018 was found; the competitors named in TechCrunch 2021 (DouxMatok, MycoTechnology, Sensient) are three years later, and Better Juice and Bonumose were founded in 2017 and 2016 but only in undated pages.
